wall_clock_steps_during_run.how_known: a monitor sampling wall-minus-monotonic offset every 20 ms (logging any change above 1 ms) ran from 2026-11-11T06:56:50Z, as the suite started, until about 2026-11-11T07:48Z, after the suite and before the reruns; it was stopped by signal, so it wrote no end line. It logged one pair: an offset change of -4.031 ms at 07:45:25.130Z and +4.031 ms 20 ms later, returning to the earlier offset; this matches a 4 ms delay between the monitor's two clock reads in one sample and is not a sustained backward step, but the monitor cannot distinguish the two. The systemd journal count of 'Time jumped backwards' entries for this boot was 3 before and 3 after (latest at 16:14 local time on 2026-11-10, before the run). The reruns were not monitored. The only failure is outside the clock-ordering files, so its classification does not depend on this.

reruns: the one failure was rerun alone 3 times against the run's own database with the same environment except MEMBRAIN_REQUIRE_BROWSER (not set by the rerun script, as in earlier reruns): it failed in 3 of 3 attempts with the same assertion; the database stopped afterwards
cleanup: the run's database, pytest, .agent-memory-recovery and rerun-0..2 directories were removed after the database was confirmed stopped; junit.xml, result.json, logs and the rerun script are kept in the run directory
